relation_to_existing_deltas.nonduplicate_delta: Existing deltas establish missing typed tool/child identity capture and session-scoped effect correlation. This delta traces that same missing identity into the Global Workspace intention/reflective measurement path, where tool ownership is reconstructed from session provenance plus a time window.

source_crosschecks.finding: merken(payload) reads session_id/tool_name/tool_input/tool_response, writes durable_memory kind=ereignis, and stores provenance as hook:PostToolUse:session=<session_id>. The persisted event record does not preserve call-scoped tool_use_id or child agent_id/Agent agentId as typed identity fields.

gw_absicht reconstructs actually-fired tools by selecting all durable_memory ereignis rows in [started_at, now] whose provenance equals hook:PostToolUse:session=<session_id>, then reduces them to a set of tool names. It does not partition those observations by tool_use_id or child identity.

source_crosschecks.path: Claude Code official hooks documentation observed 2026-08-28
source_crosschecks.finding: Current documentation exposes call-scoped tool_use_id on tool hooks and agent_id on tool hooks that execute inside a subagent; Agent PostToolUse also documents tool_response.agentId. These identity surfaces can support finer provenance than the donor currently retains.

architecture_finding.consequence: If parent and/or multiple child tool events share the same session provenance and overlap the same active-turn window, gw_absicht can merge their tool observations before computing ANGEKUENDIGT_NICHT_AUSGEFUEHRT, WIRKUNG_OHNE_ANKUENDIGUNG or AUSGEFUEHRT_NICHT_ANGEKUENDIGT. That can contaminate reflective/agency measurements even when the underlying hook events carried exact invocation/child identity.

sequence: Parent turn S opens at started_at.
Child A and child B emit PostToolUse events that the donor persists only as hook:PostToolUse:session=S plus tool name.
gw_absicht selects both events by the same session provenance and time window.
The resulting werkzeuge set no longer preserves which actor/invocation produced each observation, so reflective mismatch labels can be attributed to the parent turn without exact child ownership.
mechanistic_counterexample.claim_boundary: This is a structural provenance-collapse construction. Actual collision frequency and exact session-id behavior on the installed target runtime remain unobserved.

counterhypotheses: The installed host may serialize all relevant tool activity or assign child executions distinct session_id values, preventing this collision in practice.
A host-private/global hook or coordinator path outside the pinned donor may already preserve child/invocation identity before these records are consumed.

Some intended Global Workspace metrics may deliberately aggregate child activity at parent-turn scope; even then, explicit actor/invocation provenance is still required so aggregation is a declared projection rather than irreversible source loss.

frankenstein_2_action.projection_rule: Global Workspace/GWT may intentionally aggregate parent and child activity, but aggregation must occur after exact typed provenance is retained. Session_id plus time-window membership must not be the sole ownership key when finer identities are available.
frankenstein_2_action.required_nonprovider_test: Synthetic same-session fixture with disjoint parent/child or child-A/child-B PostToolUse identities inside one turn window; assert raw typed events remain separable and gw_absicht/GWT projection only merges them under an explicit declared aggregation rule.
